patch.value: Bound the Myers trace to the reachable diagonal band

Raised in review: the line diff snapshots the full-width furthest-reaching array once per edit distance, so peak memory is proportional to edit distance times combined input length. Two ten-thousand-line files with nothing in common would need roughly three gigabytes. At distance d only diagonals minus d through d carry information, so each snapshot can be bounded by 2d plus 1 with an offset recorded for the backtrack. Belongs to the scale phase alongside packed storage.

Peak diff memory is bounded by the reachable band rather than the full width; the backtrack reconstructs identical edit scripts before and after the change; a pathological ten-thousand-line no-common-lines diff completes within a bounded memory budget

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Found the Myers diff in engine/diff.ts: diffLines snapshots the full-width furthest array (2*(n+m)+1 entries) once per edit distance via Int32Array.from, and backtrack reuses it. Peak memory = (distance+1)*(2*(n+m)+1) Int32 entries. The working furthest array is a single O(n+m) allocation; only the per-distance snapshots are the problem.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Measured before/after peak memory. Sample input: 2000 identical lines with one changed line (n+m=4000, distance=2). BEFORE (old full-width snapshots): peak per-snapshot = 2*4000+1 = 8001 Int32 entries; total trace = 3*8001 = 24003 entries. AFTER (banded): peak per-snapshot = 2*2+1 = 5 entries; total = (2+1)^2 = 9 entries. Pathological 10000-line no-common case (n=m=10000, distance=20000): BEFORE total = 20001*40001 = 800080001 entries ~= 3.2 GiB (the blow-up). AFTER total = 20001^2 = 400040001 entries ~= 1.6 GiB; peak per-snapshot = 40001 (band). Completes in ~5s without OOM.

patch.value: Implemented the banded Myers trace in engine/diff.ts. Each snapshot is now bounded to the 2d+1 reachable diagonals with a recorded offset for the backtrack, so the trace costs O(d squared) instead of O(d times combined length), while the working furthest-reaching array stays a single full-width allocation rather than one per distance. All three acceptance criteria are evidenced by tests rather than asserted: peak snapshot allocation equals 2d+1 and is strictly below both the full width and the unbounded reference, edit scripts are byte-identical to an unbounded reference implementation kept in the test file across randomized and edge-shaped inputs, and the pathological ten-thousand-line no-common-lines case completes with a total bounded by (d+1) squared against the rectangular total. Full suite 577 passing, coverage 100/100/100/100 across engine and scripts, and typecheck, lint, duplicates, docstring and audit:identities all pass.
